newsitem.title: USA: AMBAC says has $6.8 mln annual Miami debt exposure.
newsitem.headline: AMBAC says has $6.8 mln annual Miami debt exposure.

text.p: AMBAC Indemnity Corp, a unit of AMBAC Inc, said Friday it has a "nominal" amount of annual debt service exposure to Miami bonds of $6.8 million.

In a statement describing the bond insurance company's exposure to Miami's fiscal crisis, AMBAC said it "reassured holders of its insured Miami bonds that it does not foresee any disruption in debt service payments by the city, despite Miami's publicized financial difficulties."
AMBAC said it has $85 million in net par exposure to Miami, but would not immediately be on the hook for that amount in the event the city defaulted.
Bond insurers guarantee only that principal and interest payments on outstanding bonds be paid as they come due, not all at once.

In any event, AMBAC said it does not believe default is likely. "AMBAC believes that the city of Miami and the state of Florida, under the auspices of the Emergency Financial Control Board, will develop an effective plan for solving any cash flow problems and budgetary imbalances."
AMBAC said situations like Miami, which is facing a $68 million shortfall in its $275 million budget, have in the past spurred greater demand for bond insurance.
